hero.eyebrow: CLOSURE-DRIVEN SOFTWARE DEVELOPMENT · ADVANCED PRACTITIONER DRAFT
hero.headline: Turn uncertainty into executable evidence before it hardens into architecture.
hero.support: A Boundary-First engineering method for progressively tightening domain uncertainty, exposing invariants and responsibility, building the delivery path early, and letting working artifacts correct the plan.

definition.title: Delivery is progressive closure under uncertainty.
definition.body: Backlogs, refinement, prototypes, tests, deployments, and working increments are useful when they reduce consequential uncertainty. The method treats each artifact as a bounded claim about the domain and asks execution to confirm, refine, or falsify that claim.
definition.maxim: Own the problem complexity; do not create code complexity.

steps.name: Discover
steps.question: What is the domain actually trying to change, preserve, or recognize?
steps.witness: named actors, artifacts, distinctions, and failure cases

steps.name: Bound
steps.question: What must be true for this increment to be safe enough to commit to implementation?
steps.witness: declared scope, invariants, dependencies, and unresolved questions

steps.name: Skeleton
steps.question: What is the smallest end-to-end path that can expose integration, ownership, environment, and delivery failure?
steps.witness: one executable path from real input to recognizable output

steps.name: Execute
steps.question: What does the working artifact reveal that the plan could not?
steps.witness: running behavior, logs, tests, and stakeholder interaction

steps.name: Witness
steps.question: Who or what can verify that the domain condition was actually satisfied?
steps.witness: domain-recognized evidence rather than ticket state alone

steps.name: Repair or promote
steps.question: Which defects require another loop, and which findings are stable enough to become a stronger commitment?
steps.witness: repaired boundary, promoted rule, or explicitly retained uncertainty

certainty.title: Implementation readiness is an intersection, not a feeling.
certainty.body: A task is ready when the domain cone of certainty and the executable cone of certainty overlap at the granularity of the commitment being made. The method does not require complete knowledge; it requires enough knowledge for the next irreversible or expensive decision.
executableCone: the smallest delivery path is known
the environment can run the increment

deliverySkeleton.title: Build the path that can tell the truth.
deliverySkeleton.body: Establish delivery structure early enough that integration, deployment, ownership, environment, and operational blockers can falsify the plan before large amounts of code accumulate.
requirements: accept one real or representative input
preserve the distinctions the increment depends on
produce a domain-recognized output or witness
expose at least one failure path
include enough observation to diagnose the failure
identify who can repair the path

workedExample.title: Worked example: “Export the current case list.”
workedExample.request: A user asks for a CSV export button on a case-management dashboard. The UI request is simple; the domain commitment is not.
hiddenDistinctions: all cases or only the currently filtered result set
visible fields versus fields the user is not authorized to export
current values versus historically reconstructed values
display labels versus stable machine identifiers
screen ordering versus deterministic export ordering
small synchronous exports versus large asynchronous jobs
successful generation versus successful delivery to the requester
temporary artifact retention and deletion obligations
whether the export itself requires an audit record
smallestSkeleton: one audit witness linking requester, scope, time, and artifact
workedExample.closureCheck: The ticket is not closed merely because a file downloads. Closure requires agreement that the exported set is the intended set, protected fields remain protected, the output is reconstructable, failures are visible, and the artifact's lifecycle has an owner.
workedExample.lesson: The working slice is not a miniature final system. It is an instrument for discovering which distinctions the final system must preserve.

validation.title: Treat the method as a testable engineering claim.
evidenceTargets: unresolved requirement count at implementation start
rework caused by missed domain distinctions
escaped defects attributable to representation or boundary errors
decision latency for unresolved ownership or authority
stakeholder agreement on closure conditions before and after execution
validation.comparisonShape: Compare a baseline delivery process and a closure-driven process on similarly bounded increments, then inspect whether early executable witnesses reduce late boundary discovery without imposing disproportionate analysis cost.
validation.claimRule: These are measurement targets and hypotheses for validation, not published performance results.

claimBoundary.title: Draft method, not a universal delivery law.
safe: Closure-Driven Software Development is a current Boundary First Labs engineering method under active refinement.
The method can be evaluated through bounded delivery experiments and comparative project evidence.

Its practices intentionally overlap with established Agile, Lean, systems engineering, DevOps, formal methods, domain modeling, testing, and reliability disciplines where those disciplines already solve the problem.
notEstablished: that the method outperforms established software delivery approaches in general
that every project should use the same amount of boundary analysis
that closure can eliminate uncertainty rather than bound and expose it
that a successful worked example constitutes empirical validation

closing.title: Do not ask the plan to predict what execution can reveal sooner.
closing.finalLine: Tighten the boundary, build the witness, let the artifact answer, then repair or promote.
